title: False positive — JSON response field reorder classified as a breaking change
expected_feedback: No violations, and specifically not a breaking change. RFC 8259 §1 defines a JSON object as an unordered collection of name/value pairs, so key order is not part of the contract and every spec-conformant consumer is unaffected. The reorder does change the serialized byte sequence, because encoding/json emits struct fields in declaration order, but that only matters when a named consumer parses positionally or by string prefix, or when a byte-exact artifact derives from the raw body (HMAC, response signature, content-addressed cache key, an ETag hashed from the body, or a golden-file test). The consumer audit in this snippet rules out both, so S5 classifies the change as non-breaking and no migration plan or version bump is required. Reporting this as breaking by default is a false positive that generates noise on routine refactors. Had a positional consumer existed, the correct report names that consumer and records its non-conformance — it does not generalize into a rule about JSON.
must_not_flag: a struct field reorder reported as a breaking API change with no positional consumer and no body digest
a demand for a version bump or migration plan for a pure field reorder
